title: The Battle of Dien Bien Phu
subject: histoire
description: From **March 13** to **May 7, 1954**, a French army besieged in a basin in North Vietnam capitulated to the Viet-Minh. The defeat spells the end of French Indochina.

hero.hook: In a basin of Vietnam, a colonial army discovers that the jungle can defeat aviation.

blocks.text: **May 7, 1954**, in a valley in North Vietnam, a European colonial army capitulates. Facing it: the Viet-Minh, the Vietnamese independence movement. **Diên Biên Phu** is not only a French disaster. This is the signal that the colonial era is faltering, in the midst of the Cold War.
How did a former history professor, General **Võ Nguyên Giáp**, defeat a modern army? Through logistics, patience, and by turning their own certainty of superiority against the French.

Since the 1880s, France has dominated Indochina, now Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia. In **September 1945**, , founder of the Viet-Minh, proclaimed independence. Paris refuses. The Indochina War begins: on one side the French expeditionary force, with tanks and planes; on the other the Viet-Minh and its  in , North Vietnam. [[Ho Chi Minh]] [[Guerrilla warfare]] [[Tonkin]]

blocks.caption: General Võ Nguyên Giáp, Viet-Minh strategist.

blocks.text: never attended military school. He said he learned strategy by reading Napoleon's campaigns in the Hanoi library. [[General Võ Nguyên Giáp]]

Giáp thinks of the war in stages: clandestinity, mobile guerrilla warfare, then general offensive. In 1953, he judged his army ready. The French, for their part, are looking for the terrain for a decisive battle.

General **Henry Navarre**, head of French forces in Indochina, launches **Operation Castor**: install an air-land base in Diên Bien Phu to force the Viet-Minh to attack it. In **November 1953**, parachutists jumped into the basin. The support points bear women's names: Béatrice, Gabrielle, Éliane...

The French calculation: the enemy will never be able to hoist heavy artillery in the jungle. Error. Tens of thousands of porters transport cannons and ammunition on the backs of men and reinforced bicycles. The pieces are camouflaged on the ridges which dominate the camp.

**March 13, 1954**, the flood begins. The airstrip was destroyed in the first hours. Colonel **Charles Piroth**, who had promised to silence the enemy artillery, commits suicide. The siege lasts **55 days**. Under the , these torrential rains of Asia, the basin becomes a quagmire. The Viet Minh trenches get closer every night. [[monsoon]]
On the first day, the French fired **6 000** shells. Giáp's artillery fired **9 000**: a power that the general staff considered impossible for a guerrilla army.
The United States refuses a massive air intervention. On **7 May**, after hand-to-hand combat on the Éliane support point, the ceasefire was sounded.

The  (July 1954) marked the French departure. Vietnam is divided at the **17th parallel**. More than **2,000** dead on the French side, **11,000** prisoners; less than **4 000** will return. A few months later, Algeria was set ablaze. The United States is gradually getting involved in what will become the . [[Geneva agreements]] [[Vietnam War]]

blocks.text: Diên Bien Phu (**March 13 - May 7, 1954**) shows that people's logistics and patient strategy can defeat a modern colonial army.
